historical_references.reference: Al-Shabi, a famous poet from Kufa, was a contemporary of Imam Ali ibn Abu Talib. His poetry was notable for its scathing criticism of the Umayyad caliphs, who ruled from Damascus.
historical_references.context: The Umayyad Caliphate was a major political power in the Islamic world during this period. Al-Shabi's poetry reflected the discontent of many Muslims with the ruling dynasty and its perceived corruption and deviation from the teachings of the prophet Muhammad.

historical_references.reference: Another historical figure named Al-Shabi was a prominent scholar and theologian during the Abbasid Caliphate in the 9th century CE. He was known for his expertise in Islamic jurisprudence and was a prominent figure in the development of the Shafi'i school of law.
historical_references.context: The Abbasid Caliphate was the dominant political and cultural power in the Islamic world during this period. Al-Shabi's contributions to Islamic jurisprudence helped shape the legal framework of the Islamic world and continue to be influential in modern Islamic legal thought.
